title: dbt lineage graphs
description: Adds dbt fences to the flow diagrams: a lineage written one chain of -> per line, with sources, seeds, snapshots, exposures and metrics by prefix, a model's layer from its name and its materialization, contract or former name in brackets. Each node shows its kind or materialization as an icon and its layer as a coloured edge, and a change between versions marks models renamed (with was), re-materialized (table → incremental) or moved in the lineage, besides new and removed ones. The README, the writing-slides skill and a VS Code snippet document it.

## Moving payments into their own model let orders go incremental
- A node is a model unless `source:`, `seed:`, `snapshot:`, `exposure:` or `metric:` comes first; a name with a dot, `shop.orders`, is a source.
- A model's layer comes from its prefix, `stg_`, `int_`, or `fct_`, `dim_` and the like, and colours its left edge. Keep the project's own names; do not rename models for the slide.

- In brackets, on any mention of a node: its materialization (`view`, `table`, `incremental`, `ephemeral`, `materialized_view`, `dynamic_table`), `contract`, and `was old_name` for a rename. Write a rename with `was`, never as a removal and an addition: the node then moves as itself, marked Renamed, with its old name under the new one.
- Changed covers a new materialization, drawn as `table → incremental`, and a contract added or dropped. Moved means a model stopped reading from a node that is still there.
- `#` starts a comment. `direction=`, `duration=` and `edges=` work as in `flow`.
Model names are wider than flowchart labels, so a lineage fits less:
| Lineage | Fits at full size | One more |
| Left to right | 3 ranks of names like `stg_payments`, 4 of short ones | 4 shrink to 88% |
| Several models into one | 5 stacked, 4 under a two-line headline | 5 shrink to 92% |
Show the models the change touches and their direct neighbours, not the whole project: sources can often go, since the staging models name them.

added: A `dbt` fence draws a dbt project's lineage, one chain of `->` per line, and animates a change to it like a `flow` fence. Each node shows what it is (a source, a seed, a snapshot, an exposure, a metric, or a model by its materialization) and a model's layer in the colour of its left edge.
| `source:`, `seed:`, `snapshot:`      | The kind of node, as are `exposure:` and `metric:`; a model by default |
| `shop.orders`                        | A source, since its name has a dot                                     |
| `stg_`, `int_`, `fct_` or `dim_`     | The model's layer: staging, intermediate or mart                       |
| `(table)`, `(incremental)` and so on | Its materialization; also `view`, `ephemeral`, `materialized_view`     |
| `(contract)`                         | An enforced contract, shown as a shield                                |
| `(was orders)`                       | Renamed from `orders`: it moves as the same node, marked Renamed       |

Annotations can go on any mention of a node and combine: `(incremental, contract)`. Changed covers a new materialization, shown as `table → incremental`, and a contract added or dropped. Moved means a model no longer reads from a node that is still there, as `fct_orders` above stops reading `stg_payments`. `direction=`, `duration=` and `edges=` after the language work as in a `flow` fence. Three ranks of model names fit side by side, and four or five models stacked in one. In VS Code, typing `dbt` in a slide offers a fence to start from.
